title: Complexity of Independent Feedback Vertex Set for H-free graphs (linear forest cases)
statement_text: Only the cases where $H$ is a linear forest, that is, a disjoint union of paths, remain open for the complexity classification of \textsc{Independent Feedback Vertex Set} on $H$-free graphs. In particular, the case where $H$ is a single path $P_h$ with $h \geq 6$ has not yet been resolved.
context_text: A feedback vertex set of $G$ is a set $S$ of vertices such that $G-S$ is a forest; Independent Feedback Vertex Set asks, given $G$ and $k$, whether $G$ has a feedback vertex set of size at most $k$ that is an independent set. Equivalently, it asks for a proper 3-colouring in which one colour class has at most $k$ vertices and the other two classes induce a forest; graphs having an independent feedback vertex set are called near-bipartite, and recognising them is NP-complete. $G$ is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and $P_h$ is the path on $h$ vertices. The authors prove that the problem (even Near-Bipartiteness) is NP-complete on line graphs, hence on $H$-free graphs whenever $H$ contains a claw, and NP-complete on graphs of arbitrarily large girth, hence whenever $H$ contains a cycle. Tamura et al. solved it in polynomial time for $P_4$-free graphs (cographs), and the main result of the paper is a polynomial-time algorithm for $P_5$-free graphs (also for Independent Odd Cycle Transversal). For comparison, 3-Colouring is polynomial on $P_r$-free graphs for $r\le7$ and open for $r\ge8$; no NP-hardness is known for these problems on $P_r$-free graphs, and the authors ask whether Near-Bipartiteness on $P_r$-free graphs is polynomially equivalent to 3-Colouring on $P_{f(r)}$-free graphs for some function $f$.
